plain_english_title: Gunshot & Shrapnel Wounds Rated Only as a 0% or 10% Skin Scar
what_this_means: When a bullet or explosive fragment passes into or through the body, it can cause up to three distinct types of lasting disability: (1) a surface skin scar, (2) underlying muscle damage causing weakness or early fatigue, and (3) nerve damage causing numbness or tingling. In many older rating decisions, VA assigned only a 0% or 10% skin-scar code (Diagnostic Codes 7800–7805) without evaluating whether the wound damaged an underlying muscle group (Diagnostic Codes 5301–5323) or peripheral nerve.
record_clues: A VA Rating Code Sheet showing 0% or 10% under Diagnostic Code 7800, 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805 for a gunshot wound (GSW) or shrapnel/fragment wound (SFW), with no 5300-series muscle code listed.
A Purple Heart on a DD-214, casualty report, or military award citation.

Service hospital, surgical, or separation exam notes mentioning 'through-and-through' (T&T), 'debridement' (surgical cleaning of damaged deep tissue), 'retained metallic fragments' on X-ray, 'fascia defect', or muscle weakness/atrophy.
important_cautions: Exact decision dates matter: VA overhauled the muscle-injury regulation (38 C.F.R. § 4.56) effective July 3, 1997 (published June 3, 1997 at 62 FR 30235), and updated skin-scar rules in 2002, 2008, and 2018. Meanwhile, a September 29, 2025 painful-scars notice (90 FR 46542) is a proposed rule only and is NOT enacted law.

If hospital surgical ward charts were missing when VA first decided the claim, requesting those official inpatient records and submitting them under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) is very different from filing a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion.

Do not file a Board of Veterans' Appeals CUE motion lightly: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific prior Board issue, no further CUE motions are permitted on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Can we request my complete VA Claims File (C-file), including every historical internal VA Rating Code Sheet, to see the exact 4-digit Diagnostic Codes assigned?
Did VA have my military inpatient surgical / evacuation hospital packet—not just my outpatient health jacket—when it issued the original scar rating (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c))?
Based on the exact version of 38 C.F.R. § 4.56 in effect on my decision date, do my service records document muscle-group involvement or nerve symptoms separate from the surface skin scar?
Would an additional muscle or nerve rating have changed my combined monthly compensation percentage on that date under VA's Combined Ratings Table (38 C.F.R. § 4.25)?
